findings.title: Reject signatures whose length differs from the expected JOSE length
findings.body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER copies exactly signLength bytes without checking signature.length. An oversized input is therefore accepted and its suffix silently discarded, producing the same DER signature as the valid prefix. An undersized input instead throws an unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException rather than the declared IOException. JOSE ECDSA signatures must have exactly the expected fixed length; validate the input length before copying so malformed signatures cannot be normalized into valid ones.

findings.title: Generate the matching EC curve for each algorithm test
findings.body: All three tests generate an EC key pair using the JCA default curve, which is P-256 on the standard JDK provider. Selecting SHA384withECDSA or SHA512withECDSA changes the digest, not the curve, so the ES384 and ES512 tests merely pad P-256 signature values to larger widths. In particular, the ES512 test never exercises a real P-521 signature or the long-form ASN.1 sequence length that it requires. Initialize the generator with secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1 respectively, and verify the reconstructed DER signature with JCA rather than relying only on a round trip through the two new conversion methods.
